mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% annualized over the past month signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If CPIAUCSL rises above 2% annualized and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of the cases.

mechanism_narrative: A significant decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points over the past two months signals a tightening labor market, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE decreases by more than 0.5pp and S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are negative in more than 40% of the cases.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over the past three months indicates strong consumer demand, which drives corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If RSAFS increases consistently and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of the cases.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% over the past month signals a weakening supply side, which can lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days due to concerns about economic slowdown.
failure_condition: If INDPRO decreases by more than 1% and S&P 500 forward 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the cases.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) is rising, the combination signals a restrictive monetary policy environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS > 4% and CPIAUCSL is rising, but S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of the cases.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 jobs over the past month, coupled with a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.3 percentage points, signals a strong labor market, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 200k and UNRATE decreases > 0.3pp in 1 month
failure_condition: If PAYEMS increases by more than 200k and UNRATE decreases by more than 0.3pp, but S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are negative in more than 40% of the cases.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 10% over the past two months signals a strong demand for housing, which is a leading indicator of economic growth and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If HOUST increases by more than 10% and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of the cases.

mechanism_narrative: When real GDP (GDPC1) growth slows to less than 1% quarter-over-quarter and industrial production (INDPRO) decreases by more than 0.5% month-over-month, it signals a weakening supply side and economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 growth < 1% QoQ and INDPRO decreases > 0.5% MoM
failure_condition: If GDPC1 growth is less than 1% QoQ and INDPRO decreases by more than 0.5% MoM, but S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of the cases.
